newsitem.title: USA: Miami eyes debt escrow requirement by Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: Miami eyes debt escrow requirement by Feb 28.

text.p: Miami expects to set up an escrow account to segregate and protect debt service revenues by the end of February, a member of the state-appointed oversight board said Tuesday.

The executive order that Florida's governor signed in December, which appointed the oversight board, required that Miami's "pledged revenues for principal and interest payments of outstanding debt shall be placed with a third party trustee to ensure that all debt obligations of the city will be met."
Oversight board member Adolfo Henriques said Tuesday that had not yet been done, and could not be "until we have a handle on the cash flows."
The city is expected to finish its cash flow estimates by the end of February, and the escrow account will be established "during this month," Henriques said.
He said the city has met all its debt service payments and that there was no danger of a default because "We don't expect any type of cash crunch."
According to city figures reported to the board, Miami owes debt service payments of a little over $42 million in fiscal 1997, which began Oct 1, 1996.
The city currently has about $120 million cash on hand, Henriques said.

He said the city probably would establish the escrow account with First Union Corp, which already handles some city accounts, or the Bank of New York Co Inc, which acts as trustee for some of Miami's bonds.
